title: Robust Causal Discovery in Real-World Time Series with Power-Laws
claim: Transform raw noisy signals into spectral power-law features per window, then run a standard causal test on those features to recover structure.
layout: 4 numbered stages stacked top-to-bottom, elbow arrows linking, green dashed windows
description: A vertical, four-step pipeline with black numbered circles. Step 1 is a line plot of two noisy time series, x1 in blue and x2 in orange, over time 0 to 1000. Green dashed boxes mark overlapping windows, and one window is labeled k. Gray lines connect that window to step 2. Step 2 is a log-log style scatter of power spectrum against frequency, with fitted blue and orange lines. A legend gives the amplitude and exponent values a_k and λ_k for each series. Step 3 stacks two time-series panels for the derived amplitude series a1, a2 and exponent series λ1, λ2. Black elbow arrows carry the flow down and left. Step 4 is a 'Causal Discovery' box with a block arrow to a two-node estimated causal graph, 1 pointing to 2.
caption: Schematic illustration of the proposed methodology. The original time series, here $x_1$ and $x_2$, are segmented into overlapping windows (step \circledtext*[height=1.8ex,charshrink=0.65]{1}). Then, for each window $k$, the amplitudes ($a^k_1$, $a^k_2$) and the exponents ($\lambda^k_1$, $\lambda^k_2$) of the power-law distributed spectra are computed (step \circledtext*[height=1.8ex,charshrink=0.65]{2}). These give rise to new, multi-dimensional, time series: ($a_1$,$\boldsymbol{\lambda}_1$) for $x_1$ and ($a_2$,$\boldsymbol{\lambda}_2$) for $x_2$ respectively (step \circledtext*[height=1.8ex,charshrink=0.65]{3}). Finally, multivariate Granger causality tests are performed on these new series, and the causal graph is constructed (step \circledtext*[height=1.8ex,charshrink=0.65]{4}).
abstract: Exploring causal relationships in stochastic time series is a challenging yet crucial task with a vast range of applications, including finance, economics, neuroscience, and climate science. Many algorithms for Causal Discovery (CD) have been proposed; however, they often exhibit a high sensitivity to noise, resulting in spurious causal inferences in real data. In this paper, we observe that the frequency spectra of many real-world time series follow a power-law distribution, notably due to an inherent self-organizing behavior. Leveraging this insight, we build a robust CD method based on the extraction of power-law spectral features that amplify genuine causal signals. Our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art alternatives on both synthetic benchmarks and real-world datasets with known causal structures, demonstrating its robustness and practical relevance.
